summary: The Farallon Islands light (1855), 30 miles off San Francisco: a keepers' island with a fog siren, and a wildlife refuge closed to the public.

access.note: The refuge is closed to the public due to the sensitivity of wildlife.

facts.agency: Farallon Islands National Wildlife Refuge (U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service)

events.note: Tower built on the summit; too small for a first-order lens and rebuilt (Bache visit, 5 July 1855).
First lit 1 January 1856 according to LighthouseFriends (the archive gives 1855).
Ship Lucas foundered on the island in dense fog.
Bache's whistle on the blowhole, built 1858-59 (Johnson, 1889).
A storm blew the blowhole chimney off its foundation and ended the whistle.
Steam siren began service on 20 September 1880.
Weather Bureau radio station established on the island.
Siren converted from steam to oil.
Farallon Islands National Wildlife Refuge established.
Navy set up a radio station on the island.
Air diaphone replaced the steam siren.
Coast Guard took over the lighthouse.
Tower top and lens removed; the shortened tower took an automated aero beacon (plaque date 1969, per LighthouseFriends).
Coast Guard presence ended; the light is automated (LighthouseFriends).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The archive dates the establishment and original lens to 1855; LighthouseFriends gives the first lighting as 1 January 1856, and Wikipedia (lead only) says December 1855. The story gives the 1855 completion and the 1856 first lighting; the day is not settled.

LighthouseFriends dates the reconstruction (lantern and lens removed) to 1969 from a plaque, and the Coast Guard presence ends in 1972. Both dates can hold: the work came first and automation was completed later.

notes_for_editor: Unresolved: (1) Tower height: the archive gives 29 feet to the lantern base (current shape: conical without lantern); Putnam (1917) gives 41 feet; the story gives the archive figure and notes Putnam's. (2) Keepers' quarters year: archive 1876; LighthouseFriends 1878 (first duplex) and 1880 (second). Story uses LighthouseFriends's dates. (3) Range: the 1925 Bulletin gives a geographical range of 26 miles; the record gives 14 nautical miles (nominal, from a secondary list). Not changed in the record. (4) Distance from the Golden Gate: 30 miles (USFWS, from the Golden Gate Bridge) and 23 miles (Putnam, 1917, from the Golden Gate). (5) Who operates the light today is not stated in the sources read (USFWS page says closed to the public; the archive says active). The story does not name an operator. (6) The Royal Beeman boat trip and the Cameron letter rest on LighthouseFriends, which quotes the San Francisco Call; one Chronicling America search for 'Royal Beeman' with 'Farallon' in California papers, 1898-1899, returned no hits; the Cameron letter was not checked. (7) The 1929 Kunder quote is LighthouseFriends's citation of a 1929 newspaper; not checked. (8) Bache's 1855 visit and the mule come from LighthouseFriends; Bache's report was not read. (9) The 1858 Lucas wreck rests on LighthouseFriends alone. (10) Bulletin 1916 reads 'since about ] 898' (OCR); the story says 'since about 1898' using the OCR-quoted sentence; the 1898 year is an inference from an OCR '] 898'. (11) The Bulletin 1920 passage about a former keeper's report was too garbled to use. (12) The North Farallon light and fog station (Bulletin 1913 appropriation) is a different station and is not used here. (13) Fog-siren hours from the Lighthouse Board: printed pages unconfirmed; scan pages cited. (14) Roster counts (from the 312-line archive roster): 35 head keepers, 7 acting keepers, 217 assistants, 3 laborers, 50 Coast Guard entries. (15) Post-1960 names appear only in the keeper rows, not in the prose. (16) Newspapers: one search (Royal Beeman) returned no hits; no other newspaper search was made for this station. (17) Fiscal years are now labelled in the story (fiscal year ending June, per the report's own title). (18) Johnson (1889) and Putnam (1917) footnotes no longer say 'general context' or 'general history': the facts cited are about this station. (19) The 1925 Bulletin passage is on PDF p. 22; note 16 is corrected to match note 8. (20) Roster counts from roster.py: 35 head, 6 acting plus 1 temporary, 217 assistants (49 first, 77 second, 91 third), 3 laborers, 50 Coast Guard = 312. (21) Copyrighted LighthouseFriends wording is paraphrased; the only quoted LighthouseFriends phrases are short.
